title: Sitting in with Duke Ellington's band at the Zanzibar
summary: Friendship with Ben Webster leads Leeman to sit in for the ailing Sonny Greer on the last sets at the Zanzibar.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Uh huh. These are beautiful, this is a matter of record. How did you happen to know Bill, how did you happen to recommend him?
I was just around Duke's band every minute I had, and then ...
Well, we talked before, Cliff, and you told me -- did you know him in Kansas City?

I saw him in Kansas City, but I didn't go up to him. He came through at that theatre, the Tower Theatre, and I saw him playing there, and then when I went to see Duke, I talked to Ben -- we had another mutual friend -- we worked together so much after that. Anyway, Ben and I kept getting to be better friends and so forth, and Sonny was having a bad time, he was sick with something --

And Sonny was sick, and I was off for a week or two, and I would go in every night to see Duke's band -- sometimes Duke would be there, he'd be off the stand, and I'd be down at the bar downstairs, and Ben would say come on upstairs and play so Sonny could go home, you know? After their broadcast, after the broadcast.
So this was how you got to play with Duke?
So the last couple of sets at night, the last hour and a half, I'd go up there, and I knew the book.
And Ben would say get on that cymbal, which Sonny had up there -- that was the beginning of the Chinese cymbal for me except that I had had a 24-incher which I made 'Back Bay Shuffle' with.
